# DT Law

> DT Law is a solo Illinois estate planning practice in Naperville, Illinois, serving families in DuPage, Will, and Kane counties, Illinois. The firm plans for families as they really are: blended, unmarried, growing, or caring for a loved one with special needs. Services include wills, powers of attorney, revocable living trusts, special needs trusts, and guardianship. Content on this site is general information about Illinois law, not legal advice.

## Key pages

- [Services and Pricing](https://dtlaw-ep.com/services/): The Foundation Plan (flat fee), Living Trust Plan, and Special Needs Plan, what each includes, the hours each covers, and how fees work.
- [The Life Cycle of Families](https://dtlaw-ep.com/life-cycle/): Fourteen life events that call for a fresh look at an estate plan, from marriage and new children to illness, divorce, and retirement, with the documents to review for each.
- [About Yung Truong](https://dtlaw-ep.com/about/): Attorney background, education, admission, and languages (English and Vietnamese).
- [Estate Planning](https://dtlaw-ep.com/estate-planning/): Wills, powers of attorney, living wills, and revocable living trusts.
- [Special Needs Trusts](https://dtlaw-ep.com/special-needs-trusts/): Third-party and first-party (payback) special needs trusts and ABLE account guidance.
- [Guardianship](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guardianship/): Planning before a child turns 18, less restrictive alternatives, and adult guardianship, filed in DuPage, Will, and Kane counties.
- Each life event in [The Life Cycle of Families](https://dtlaw-ep.com/life-cycle/) has its own page, such as /life-cycle/divorce/ and /life-cycle/new-child/.
- [Family Plan Simulator](https://dtlaw-ep.com/planner/): A free educational tool that helps families visualize relationships and money flow. Entries stay in the visitor's own browser.
- [Guides](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/): Plain-English, illustrated guides to Illinois estate planning, special needs trusts, and guardianship, organized by life event.
  - [What happens if you die without a will in Illinois](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/die-without-a-will-illinois/): Who inherits under Illinois law when there is no will, how probate works without one, and which assets the default rules do not control.
  - [Do I need a trust in Illinois](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/do-i-need-a-trust-illinois/): Estate size and the tax lines, how a living trust differs from a will, the situations where a trust tends to help, and what a trust does not do.
  - [Marriage and your estate plan in Illinois](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/marriage-estate-plan-illinois/): What Illinois law assumes for a spouse and for an unmarried partner, who decides medical care by default, and seven documents to review.
  - [New baby: where to start in Illinois](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/new-baby-estate-plan-illinois/): How to name a guardian, who manages a child's money, how a child can inherit, and six things to put in place.
  - [Guardianship when a child turns 18](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/guardianship-timeline/): Why the process starts six to twelve months early, and the less restrictive options.
  - [Special needs trusts and inheritances](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/special-needs-trust-basics/): How a direct inheritance can affect SSI and Medicaid, and what a special needs trust does.
  - [ABA-informed IEP advocacy](https://dtlaw-ep.com/guides/aba-informed-advocacy/): What a behavior-therapy background adds at an IEP or 504 meeting.
